# {{< fa graduation-cap title="graduation cap" >}} B.S. in Environmental Studies

During my undergrad, many of the final projects were open to be creative rather than traditional, such as podcasts, videos, or blog posts versus a final exam or essay. Here is one of my projects that I'm very proud to have created.

## {{< fa video title="video" >}} Documentary on Environmental Veganism

**Below is my research-based documentary:**

::: {style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"}
<iframe
    src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/fQl_8q3BXts"
    style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%;"
    frameborder="0"
    allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
    allowfullscreen> </iframe>
:::

For my Critical Thinking course (ES 40), we were tasked to do a research project of our choice and interest throughout the entire quarter. My question was based on the small percentage of students in my environmental classes identifying as vegan or vegetarian despite studies showing the amount of water and land usage that is put into upholding the meat and dairy industry. Thus, did veganism matter in the overall context of helping the Earth, if those who studied it did not partake in it? 

**In this documentary, you'll find**:

- Student interviews
- Resources to combat food insecurity
- Free weekly community dinner
- A tour of a co-op housing focused on a plant-based diet

## {{< fa cloud title="cloud" >}} A personal data collection and an interactive plot

For a final project, we had to build an interactive plot using data we collected over the quarter. I chose to collect the dates and time I practiced yoga and the pain levels I experienced throughtout the week in terms of if I practived or not. This was a simple data collection, but was still great to use to become familiar with the R language.

**Code below**:

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, echo=TRUE}

library(tidyverse)
library()
library(janitor)
library(htmlwidgets)


mydata <- read.csv("Data.csv") |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    tooltip_text = paste0(
      "Yoga Session: ", did_you_do_yoga, "<br>",
      "Pain Level After: ", pain_level_after)
  )

p <- ggplot(mydata, aes(
  x = did_you_do_yoga,
  y = pain_level_after,
  color = pain_level_after,
  text = tooltip_text
)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  stat_summary(geom = "point", fun = mean, color = "#4a4a4a", size = 3) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#f9f871", high = "#7c3f98") +  # yellow to purple gradient
  labs(
    x = "Did You Do Yoga?",
    y = "Pain Level After Yoga",
    color = "Pain Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffe6eb", color = NA),        # baby pink background
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffffff", color = "#ffb6c1"), # white panel with pink border
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#ffccd5"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

plotly::ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") |>
  plotly::layout(hoverlabel = list(font = list(size = 14)))

```
